title: Does a wave-pinning crawler whose front is cut off re-nucleate its polarity and crawl again, or retract and die?
summary: Camley et al. (PRE 95, 012401, 2017) push a phase-field cell out by a mass-conserved bistable (wave-pinning) polarity protein, whose total C also sets a window of allowed cell area. No published cut-and-recover test of any motile model turned up. Removing the front leaves the linearly stable low state everywhere, so repair is a race against retraction rather than automatic. The linear-kinetics twin cannot polarize at all, which makes it a built-in control beyond diffusion.
experiment:
Positive control (about 20 min). Camley et al.'s crawler:
- Grid and numerics: Lx = Ly = 2.5, 256^2, semi-implicit spectral, dt = 5e-4.
- Parameters: Pe^-1 = 0.3, K = 500, chi = 0.3, rho* = 0.4, m = 0.5, C = 6, eps = 0.1, G = 18 phi^2 (1-phi)^2.
- Equations: dphi/dt = (rho - rho*)|grad phi| + chi(lap phi - G'/eps^2); d(phi rho)/dt = Pe^-1 div(phi grad rho) - K phi rho (rho - 1/2)(rho - m rho_cyt); rho_cyt = (C - int rho phi)/int phi.
- Start: a circle of R0 = 1, with rho = 0.8 on the front half plus N(0, 0.2) noise.
- Expected: a half-moon crawling straight; at chi = 0.2 it turns into circles.
- Add weak ongoing noise on rho, small enough that the undamaged twin stays straight.

Damage (about 40 min). At t = 20, on 2 seeds, each with a branched undamaged twin, erase:
- (a) a 30% sector at the leading edge;
- (b) a 30% sector at the rear.
Remove the erased matter from C: C' = C - int_cut phi(rho + rho_cyt).
Readout:
- time for the front to re-form (a connected patch with rho > 1/2);
- speed relative to the twin;
- survival or retraction;
- for (a), a 3-point noise-amplitude sweep.

Twin (about 15 min). Replace the cubic kinetics with linear relaxation at the same rate. Expect no polarity and no motion.

Scoring. Credit only re-nucleation of the front. Its later smoothing is area-preserving curvature flow (Kobayashi, Sakakibara & Uechi 2026), which counts as by construction.

Optional arm. Mori-type Hill kinetics, where the shrinking fragment's concentrating pool may destabilize the low state deterministically.

sources.cite: Camley, Zhao, Li, Levine & Rappel, Crawling and turning in a minimal reaction-diffusion cell motility model, PRE 95, 012401 (2017), arXiv:1609.01764. Abstract, equations and parameters re-opened by the synthesizer.
Mori, Jilkine & Edelstein-Keshet, Wave-pinning and cell polarity from a bistable reaction-diffusion system, Biophys J 94, 3684 (2008); opened by the motility sweep.
Kobayashi, Sakakibara & Uechi, arXiv:2601.04746 (2026): wave-pinning interfaces evolve by area-preserving curvature flow on the slow timescale; abstract opened by the motility sweep.
